turns.user_text: Name one term someone reading about tipping versus higher fixed wages would need to know, and define it. Answer in four or five sentences.
turns.model_text: One term someone reading about tipping versus higher fixed wages would need to know is "tipped minimum wage." The tipped minimum wage is the minimum hourly wage that employers are required to pay employees who receive tips, such as servers, bartenders, and hairdressers. In the United States, for example, the federal tipped minimum wage is $2.13 per hour, which is lower than the standard minimum wage of $7.25 per hour. Employers are allowed to pay tipped employees the lower rate as long as their tips, combined with the employer's contribution, bring their total hourly wage up to the standard minimum wage. This system is intended to allow employers to pass on some of the costs of paying employees to customers in the form of tips.
